thread:
Anya Patel: Quick announce — canary results for tail-steer v2 are in. This is the hybrid-rate limiter + steering eviction heuristic we tested last week. p50 ~0 change, p95 -8%, p99 -22% for our chat-heavy workloads. Token-cost delta across traffic: -9%. Rolling plan below. :tada:
Kevin Liu: woo! quick question — which workload slices showed the biggest p99 wins?
Anya Patel: Mostly multi-turn chat (avg seq len 600+) and conversational helpers. Single-shot short prompts see little change.
Maria Chen: can you paste the canary query or the dashboards? want to link in the postmortem/announce.
Anya Patel: snapshot + link from canary job: https://dash.redwood.internal/canary/2067894321 — main metrics: latency, cost, error-rate.
Kevin Liu: can you also share the config we ran?
Anya Patel: config snippet used in canary:
```
steer_v2:
  rate_mode: hybrid
  tail_threshold_ms: 1200
  eviction_alpha: 0.62
  small_batch_override: true
```
Josh Ryder: saw a small regression on tiny prompt models (p50 +3%) on 2 models. likely due to small_batch_override.
Anya Patel: good catch — that matches local bench. we'll gate small_batch_override by model-tag 'short' until we tune packer.
Maria Chen: any user-facing risk? errors or hallucinations?
Anya Patel: no error uptick in canary, no quality regressions on our eval set. safety checks passed.
deploy-bot: Deploy canary 2067894321 -> started at 2067894330, rollout=5%
sre-bot: Snapshot at +1h: p99 down 20% vs baseline, token-cost -8.5%, cpu GPU utilization +2% on canary nodes. Link: https://sre.redwood.internal/snapshots/2067894321-1h
Kevin Liu: nice. do we have a rollback key if something goes sideways?
Anya Patel: yes — rollout policy auto-rolls back at +err_rate > 0.5% absolute or p99 increase > 5% for 5m. manual rollback cmds in runbook.
Maria Chen: adding to runbook now, PR coming.
DevEx: I'll open a docs PR to call out the new knobs and recommended defaults for chat vs short prompts.
Josh Ryder: recommend we hold off global until we flip off small_batch_override for "short" models. otherwise we risk small-prompt latency regressions.
Anya Patel: agreed. plan: expand 5% -> 20% after 2h stable, then flip override for short models and continue to 100% if stable. I'll post updates here at each milestone.
Maria Chen: thanks — small action items: update runbook, docs PR, QA signoff for short-model override.
Anya Patel: TL;DR: tail-steer v2 reduces p99 by ~22% for long-chat workloads and reduces token-cost ~9%. Canary at 5%, expanding to 20% now. Monitoring 24/7 for 72h. :rocket:
